lines: A Karplus-Strong delay line tuned to pitch, with up to seven unison voices on every polyphonic channel
Tunes the delay time in whole octaves, -4 to +4, added to whatever V/OCT carries
Tunes the delay time in semitones, -7 to +7, added to whatever V/OCT carries
Sets how much of the delayed signal returns to the delay line, 0 to 50%
Sets the number of unison voices on each polyphonic channel, 1 to 7
Sets how far the unison voices are detuned from one another
Sets the level of the detuned unison voices against the centre voice
Lengthens the ring by feeding the delay line back at full level on a random proportion of samples
Sets the delay time as a pitch, 1V per octave, 0V giving C4 at 261.63Hz
Added to the FEEDBACK knob, 10V for the whole range
The signal written into the delay line; its channel count sets the polyphony
Added to the COUNT knob, one unison voice per volt
Added to the SPREAD knob, 10V for the whole range, and a negative voltage acts as its own magnitude
Added to the MIX knob, 10V for the whole range, and a negative voltage acts as its own magnitude
Added to the STRETCH knob, 10V for the whole range
The unison mix read out of the delay line, limited and with DC removed

KSDelay.notes: Parameter 7, Stretch Lock, has no widget on the panel; the line creating it is commented out in the source, so it is left untagged. The prerequisite note follows the maker's README, which says the main audio input should be triggered with noise and that the colour and duration of that burst shape the sound.

Modulates the drive through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
The audio into the filter; its channel count sets the polyphony
Modulates the cutoff frequency through its attenuverter, 1V per octave at full attenuverter
The filtered audio

Maccomo.notes: The README says the six modes are selectable by CV as well as by the knob, and the code does read a mode CV input, but no jack for it was ever placed on the panel; input 3 is therefore unreachable and untagged.

Added to the SHUFFLE PROBABILITY knob, 10V for the whole range; a polyphonic cable here lets every channel reorder independently
Added to the ACCENT A PROBABILITY knob, 10V for the whole range; a polyphonic cable here gives every channel its own chance
Added to the ACCENT A OFFSET knob, volt for volt
Added to the ACCENT B PROBABILITY knob, 10V for the whole range; a polyphonic cable here gives every channel its own chance
Added to the ACCENT B OFFSET knob, volt for volt
Added to the ACCENT RNG PROBABILITY knob, 10V for the whole range; a polyphonic cable here gives every channel its own chance
Added to the RNG MAX OFFSET knob, volt for volt
The voltage sampled into the register on each trigger
A rising edge drops the channel count back to one, and it climbs again by one on every trigger
A rising edge samples the input and moves the stored voltages along one channel

PolyShiftRegister.notes: The IN jack and the OUT jack carry whatever is patched in, most often pitch but not always, so neither is given a family. The reset and trigger jacks are the last two inputs by index and are not in panel order: input 11 is the TRIGGER jack and input 10 the RESET jack.

lines: An expander for Tyrant, placed immediately to its right, which turns Tyrant's probability decisions into polyphonic triggers
A trigger on each channel whose incoming clock pulse was skipped
A trigger on each channel whose stored voltages were reordered
A trigger on each channel that received the Accent A offset
A trigger on each channel that received the Accent B offset
A trigger on each channel that received the random accent
A trigger on every channel when Tyrant is reset
Note — the outputs stay silent unless a Tyrant is the module immediately to the left and touching it
Te.notes: Te's process does nothing unless leftExpander.module is a PolyShiftRegister, matching the README's 'must be placed to the right and touching Tyrant'.

Sets the crossover frequency, marked in Hz, from 10Hz upwards

The band below the crossover frequency
Note — the two bands sum back to a flat frequency response, so several of these can be chained to make any number of bands
A two way crossover that splits a stereo pair into low and high bands with fourth order Linkwitz-Riley filters
Sets the crossover frequency, marked in Hz, from 10Hz upwards
Attenuverts the frequency modulation input, -1 to +1
Modulates the crossover frequency through its attenuverter, 1V per octave at full attenuverter
The left channel to be split; its channel count sets the polyphony of the left outputs
The right channel to be split; its channel count sets the polyphony of the right outputs
The part of the left channel above the crossover frequency
The part of the right channel above the crossover frequency
The part of the left channel below the crossover frequency
The part of the right channel below the crossover frequency
Note — the two bands of a channel sum back to a flat frequency response, so several of these can be chained to make any number of bands
A slimline mixer that sums eight polyphonic inputs through a single attenuverter
One of the inputs into the sum, taken at unity gain
One of the inputs into the sum, taken at unity gain, despite Rack's tooltip for it reading Attenuverter
Sets the level of the summed inputs, -1 to +1, inverting the sum below zero
Added to the attenuverter, 5V for a change of one, and the total is clamped to -1 and +1

Eva.notes: The eight summing inputs and the output carry audio or CV depending on what is patched, so they are given no family. The maker's configInput call for the first input passes the output enum by mistake, so Rack shows that jack's tooltip as Attenuverter; the panel prints IN over the column.

lines: A performance controller that fades a parameter on another module between two values along an easing curve, either once on a trigger or cycling without stopping
Attenuverts the easing input, -1 to +1
Selects the easing curve: back, bounce, circ, cubic, elastic, expo, linear, quad, quart, quint or sine
Attenuverts the start value input, -1 to +1
Sets one end of the fade, -1 to +1 across the assigned parameter's range
Attenuverts the end value input, -1 to +1
Sets the other end of the fade, -1 to +1 across the assigned parameter's range
Attenuverts the duration input, -1 to +1
Sets the time taken to move from one end of the fade to the other, 0 to 2 times the clock period, and 0 to 2 seconds with nothing patched to SYNC
Selects cycling, where the value runs from one end of the fade to the other and back without stopping, or one shot, where a trigger at TRIG runs it once
Does by hand what a pulse at the SYNC input does, timing the clock period from one press to the next
Does by hand what a pulse at the TRIG input does, starting a one shot fade
Does by hand what a pulse at the PAUSE input does, stopping the fade and letting it continue
Shifts the easing curve through its attenuverter, added to the EASING SHAPE knob
Modulates the start value through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
Modulates the end value through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
Modulates the duration through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
A trigger stops the fade where it stands, and the next one lets it continue
A clock; the time between two pulses is the period the DURATION knob multiplies
In one shot mode a positive trigger runs the fade from the start value to the end value, and a negative-going trigger runs it back
The value being sent to the assigned parameter, -10V to +10V
Menu — Retrigger mode — chooses what a trigger arriving part way through a fade does; Restart begins the fade again, Ignore lets it finish
Menu — Duration Multiplier — scales the DURATION knob by 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 50.0, 100.0, 500.0 or 1000.0
Note — no parameter is controlled until one is assigned: left-click the display reading Module and Parameter, then click a knob or slider on another module; right-click that display to unassign it
Note — the curve display shows the easing currently chosen, drawn as it runs in cycle or one shot mode
Zazel.notes: Retrigger mode and Duration Multiplier are MenuLabel headings; the clickable items under them are Restart and Ignore, and 0.01 through 1000.0. The parameter assignment is a left-click and a right-click on the ParameterSelectWidget display, not a menu item.

lines: A MIDI input for 14 bit continuous controllers, pairing each of CC 0 to 31 with the CC 32 numbers higher to give finer resolution than 128 steps
The value of its own pair of CC numbers, 0-10V, or -5V to +5V when the menu is set away from unipolar
Menu — Midi 1.0 — an incoming MSB sets the coarse half of the value and clears the fine half, and the LSB that follows fills it in, as the MIDI 1.0 specification defines
Menu — No Zeroing, No Waiting — each message changes its own half of the value the moment it arrives, with nothing cleared and nothing held back
Menu — MSB waits for LSB — an incoming MSB is held back until an LSB arrives and the two are applied together; an LSB with no MSB before it changes the fine half on its own
Menu — MSB LSB pair — the value changes only once both messages of the pair have arrived
Menu — Filter Smoothing — a slider setting the time constant of the filter on every output, up to 67ms, and 33ms by default
Menu — Unipolar — switches every output between 0-10V and -5V to +5V
Note — nothing appears at the outputs until a MIDI device is chosen on the display, which carries its own menus for the driver, the device and the channel
Zilah.notes: The three parameters are reached only from the context menu and have no widget on the panel, so they are untagged. Menu item names were read from appendContextMenu in src/modules/Zilah.cpp: Midi 1.0, No Zeroing, No Waiting, MSB waits for LSB, MSB LSB pair, a Filter Smoothing slider and Unipolar. The MSB waits for LSB line trips validate_help.py's personification rule on the word 'waits', which is part of the item's printed name and cannot be reworded without falsifying it; that is the one validator hit left in this file. The MIDI device is chosen on Rack's own MidiDisplay widget on the panel, not from the module's right-click menu.

lines: A trigger sequencer with eight tracks and four pages of sixteen steps, made to be played from a MIDI grid controller
Turns that step of its track on or off; while LENGTH, EUCLIDEAN or ROTATE is armed the press sets that instead
Turns that track on or off; a track that is off sends nothing to either of its outputs
Shows that quarter of the sequence on the grid, without interrupting any track
Sets every track back to its first step
Advances every track by one step
Arms the grid so that the next step pressed becomes the last step of that track, which is what lets tracks run at different lengths
Arms MIDI learn, so that a control moved on the MIDI controller and a control then clicked here are mapped to one another
At one the main output of that track follows the programmed steps exactly; below one it is the chance that a programmed step plays, and above one it adds a chance that an unprogrammed step plays
Sets the chance that a step of that track which is not programmed plays on the alt output
Arms the grid so that the next step pressed sets the number of hits spread evenly across that track's length
Arms the grid so that pressing the first step of a track rotates its pattern one step left, and pressing the second step rotates it one step right
A rising edge advances every track by one step, and the voltage present here is what the outputs pass on, so the output pulses keep the width of the clock
A rising edge sets every track back to its first step
Passes the clock pulse through whenever the programmed step on that track plays
Passes the clock pulse through on steps of that track which are not programmed, for ghost hits and alternating voices
Menu — Use Rotary Encoders — reads the probability controls as endless encoders rather than as absolute faders
Menu — Clear all Midi Mappings — removes every mapping made by MIDI learn
Menu — Clear Midi Mapping — arms a mode in which the next control clicked here, or the next control moved on the controller, has its mapping removed
Menu — Midi Learn Parameter First — reverses the order of MIDI learn, so a control here is clicked before the controller is moved
Menu — Slow midi feedback — thins out the messages sent back to the controller
Menu — None — a slider setting the MIDI note velocity sent back for a step that is off, 0 to 127, which is what picks that pad's colour
Menu — Step — a slider setting the MIDI note velocity sent back for a programmed step, 0 to 127
Menu — Index — a slider setting the MIDI note velocity sent back for the step now playing, 0 to 127
Menu — Loop — a slider setting the MIDI note velocity sent back for the last step of a track, 0 to 127
Menu — Step & Loop — a slider setting the MIDI note velocity sent back for a step that is both programmed and the last step of its track, 0 to 127
Menu — Probability Notch Width — adds a flat zone in the middle of the main probability controls, so an imprecise fader gives exactly the programmed pattern; None 0%, Slim 20%, Mid 35% or Wide 50%
Note — a grid controller lights up only once a device is chosen in both MIDI IN and MIDI OUT; each of those displays carries its own menus for the driver, the device and the channel
Note — two grid controllers can be used, one for each half of the sixteen steps, and there is a MIDI IN and a MIDI OUT display for each of them
Note — factory MIDI mappings for the APC Mini and the Launchpad Mk3 Mini ship as module presets, listed under Factory presets in the Preset submenu of the panel menu
Note — the Launchpad Mk3 mapping needs Factory Custom Mode 3 active on the controller, which is slot 3, the User button, by default
Note — the strip marked SEQUENCE draws all sixty four steps of all eight tracks at once, with the step now playing marked on each track
Iverson.notes: Parameters 136 to 143 hold the per-track loop lengths and 168 to 175 the MIDI mapping settings; none of them has a widget on the panel, so they are untagged. Probability Notch Width is a MenuLabel heading; the items under it are None  0%, Slim  20%, Mid  35% and Wide  50%. The five velocity sliders are labelled by their parameter names None, Step, Loop, Step  & Loop and Index, and set the note velocity sent back to the controller for a pad in that state. Factory MIDI mappings are module presets under Rack's own Preset submenu, not items the maker added. The installed presets folder holds two for Iverson: APC_mini and Launchpad_Mk3_Mini.

lines: A small FM oscillator with feedback, usable as a VCO or an LFO, every instance carrying its own slight detune and its own noise floor
Multiplies the frequency by two raised to its setting, -4 to +4, for dialling an FM ratio
Raises the pitch in whole semitones, 0 to 12
Shifts the pitch in whole octaves, -5 to +5
Sets how far the FM input moves the phase, 0 to 1
Sets how much of the output is folded back into its own phase, which adds harmonics to the sine
Sets the pitch, 1V per octave; its channel count sets the polyphony
Attenuates the FM input, 10V passing it at the depth the DEPTH knob sets and 0V removing it
Attenuates the feedback, 10V passing the amount the FEEDBACK knob sets and 0V removing it
The signal that modulates the phase, plus or minus 5V for the full depth
The oscillator, plus or minus 5V before the scale and offset in the menu
Menu — Output DC Offset — a slider adding -10V to +10V to the output
Menu — Scale — a slider multiplying the output by -2 to +2
Menu — Unison — a slider trading polyphony for detuned copies of the voice, 1 to 16, summed down to one channel
Menu — Over Sample Rate — a slider running the oscillator at 1 to 8 times the sample rate, which keeps the feedback and the FM from aliasing
Menu — Default Tuning — sets what 0V at V/OCT means, choosing between Audio C4 at 261.63Hz, Clock / Lfo 2Hz and Slow Lfo 0.125Hz
Hula.notes: Parameters 5 to 9 are the unison count, oversample rate, default tuning, output offset and output scale; all five are reached only from the context menu and have no widget on the panel. The menu holds four sliders, labelled by their parameter names Output DC Offset, Scale, Unison and Over Sample Rate, then a Default Tuning heading with the items Audio C4, Clock / Lfo 2hz and Slow Lfo 0.125hz. Default Tuning is a MenuLabel heading rather than a clickable item. The maker configures DEFAULT_TUNING_PARAM with the name 'Over Sample Rate', a copy-paste from the parameter before it, so Rack shows that name twice.

Sets the cutoff frequency, marked in Hz; at C4, 261.63Hz, the filter tracks V/OCT accurately
Attenuverts the frequency modulation input, -1 to +1
Attenuverts the resonance input, -1 to +1
Sets the resonance, 0.5 to 10, self-oscillating towards the top of the range
Attenuverts the drive input, -1 to +1
Sets the drive into the filter, 0.1 to 5
Attenuverts the VCA input, -1 to +1
Sets the gain the VCA applies to the filtered signal, 0 to 2
Shifts the cutoff frequency, 1V per octave, added to the FREQUENCY knob
Modulates the resonance through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
Modulates the drive through its attenuverter, 5V at full attenuverter covering the whole range
The audio into the filter; its channel count sets the polyphony
Modulates the cutoff frequency through its attenuverter, 1V per octave at full attenuverter
Modulates the VCA gain through its attenuverter, 10V at full attenuverter adding one to the gain
A second, monophonic audio input, filtered as polyphonic channel two of the same filter
The filtered audio after the VCA, with the channel count of the polyphonic input
The filtered audio from the monophonic input after the VCA, silent until that input is patched
Note — Bascom starts as a four pole lowpass; its other modes and colourings are module presets, listed under Factory presets in the Preset submenu of the panel menu
Note — a Bascom Expander placed immediately to the right opens the filter's structure up, so that a mode and a colouring can be designed by hand
Note — only the left input is polyphonic; a signal at the right input is filtered as polyphonic channel two of the same filter
Bascom.notes: Parameters 6 to 23, 26 and 27 hold the filter design: oversampling, the pole mix coefficients, the per-stage cutoff offsets, the distortion curves and the feedback path. None has a widget on Bascom's own panel; they are set from a preset or from the Bascom Expander, so they are untagged here. The default parameter values are mix coefficients A to D at 0 and E at 1, which is the plain four pole lowpass; the shipped presets are grouped as 01 Clean, 02 Diode_Resonance, 03 Diode_Resonance_Warm, 04 OverDriven_Resonance_Warm, 05 Diode_ladder and 06 Synth. Bascom has no appendContextMenu of its own, so its presets are reached through Rack's Preset submenu. configOutput is called twice on MAIN_OUTPUT, the second time with the name Right, so both output tooltips read Right; the right input is never configured and has no name.

Sets how many samples pass between one parameter update and the next, 1 to 128
Sets how much of the signal entering the ladder is added into the output mix; the ends of its travel do nothing, because Bascom clamps the value to a narrower range

Sets how much of the second pole's output is added into the output mix; the ends of its travel do nothing, because Bascom clamps the value to a narrower range
Sets how much of the third pole's output is added into the output mix; the ends of its travel do nothing, because Bascom clamps the value to a narrower range
Sets how much of the fourth pole's output is added into the output mix; the ends of its travel do nothing, because Bascom clamps the value to a narrower range
Selects the distortion curve applied to the signal arriving at the filter

Selects the distortion curve applied to the signal entering the second pole
Selects the distortion curve applied to the signal entering the third pole
Selects the distortion curve applied to the signal entering the fourth pole

Note — the knobs do nothing unless a Bascom is the module immediately to the left; they then write straight into it, and loading a preset there reads the values back into them
Note — the expander has module presets of its own for each mode, listed under Factory presets in the Preset submenu of the panel menu
BascomExpander.notes: The pole mix knobs are configured here with a range of -32 to +32, while the Bascom parameters they write into are clamped to -18 to +18, so the ends of these knobs do nothing. No range is quoted in the lines for that reason. The expander reads module->leftExpander and does nothing unless the module there is a Bascom, so it goes to the right of the filter. It ships nineteen presets of its own for the lowpass, highpass, bandpass, notch, all pass and phaser modes at 6, 12, 18 and 24dB.

lines: A five channel mixer for audio and CV, with a choice of non-linear distortion curves on the mix
Sets the level of the input with the same number, 0 to 2

Menu — NLD TYPE — a slider picking the curve the mix is shaped by, its name printed beside it; Linear leaves the mix alone, the rest are tanh and arctan shapes and sampled circuits
Note — no DC blocking filter is applied, so the mix passes slow CV as readily as audio
Mix.notes: The README calls the mixer AC coupled; the source has the DC blocking filter commented out with the note that this lets CV pass, and the panel says nothing either way. The entry follows the code. The NLD TYPE slider prints the parameter name and the shape name together, so the curve is named on the slider itself.

lines: A random voltage generator: one trigger draws five independent random voltages and holds them, each through its own attenuverter
Selects unipolar output, 0-10V, or bipolar, -5V to +5V
Adds the slow fall of an analogue sample and hold to the held voltages
Scales the random voltage on its own output, -1 to +1, inverting it below zero
A rising edge draws a fresh random voltage for every output; the channel count of this input sets the polyphony
A random voltage held until the next trigger, drawn independently of every other output
Note — nothing comes out until a trigger is patched; the trigger input sets the channel count, and with it unpatched every output is silent
Bose.notes: The composite takes its channel count from the trigger input, so with nothing patched there the loop never runs and every output is set to zero channels.

lines: A transposer for V/Oct signals: triggers step the transposition up or down by a set interval, wrapped to stay inside one octave
Sets the interval each trigger transposes by, -12 to +12 semitones; 7 walks the circle of fifths
A rising edge lowers the transposition by the SHIFT interval, wrapped back inside the octave
A rising edge raises the transposition by the SHIFT interval, wrapped back inside the octave
A rising edge returns the transposition to zero
A V/Oct signal to be transposed, polyphonic
The signal from its own input with the current transposition added
Note — the display shows the current transposition in semitones
A voltage controlled envelope generator with a stereo VCA, with a gate output for each stage and timing curves modelled on the CEM3310
Selects the shape: ADSR, AD with no sustain and both falling stages timed by DECAY, or AR with a full sustain and both falling stages timed by RELEASE
When on, a trigger at TRIG restarts the attack from the level the envelope has reached
When on, the envelope is driven quickly to zero before each attack stage
When on, the envelope retriggers itself whenever it completes, and runs without a gate
Sets the attack time, 1.2ms to 80 seconds
Attenuates the attack CV input, 0 to 1
Sets the decay time, 1.2ms to 80 seconds
Attenuates the decay CV input, 0 to 1
Sets the level held while the gate stays high, 0 to 1
Attenuates the sustain CV input, 0 to 1
Sets the release time, 1.2ms to 80 seconds
Attenuates the release CV input, 0 to 1
Modulates the attack time through its attenuator, 10V covering the whole range
Modulates the decay time through its attenuator, 10V covering the whole range
Modulates the sustain level through its attenuator, 10V covering the whole range
Modulates the release time through its attenuator, 10V covering the whole range
The left audio into the VCA
The right audio into the VCA
A rising edge restarts the attack when RETRIG is on
A high gate runs the envelope through attack, decay and sustain, and a low gate starts the release; its channel count sets the polyphony
10V for as long as the envelope is in its attack stage
10V for as long as the envelope is in its decay stage
10V for as long as the envelope is in its sustain stage

The left input multiplied by the envelope
The right input multiplied by the envelope

Menu — Waveshaping — runs the VCA outputs through a curve sampled from a hardware VCA, a different curve on the left and the right
Farini.notes: Parameter 12 is the waveshaping switch, reached only from the context menu, so it is untagged.

lines: Five separate one in, one out mults, each with a text field for a label, for naming the connections into and out of a group of modules
The signal passed to its own output, polyphonic
Carries the signal from its own input unchanged, with the same channel count
Note — each pair has a text field for a label; click it and type, and the text is saved with the patch
Thru.notes: The jacks carry whatever is patched through them, so they are given no family.

lines: A slim text panel for keeping notes beside a patch; the text is saved and loaded with the patch
Note — click the display and type; the field holds a single line of text, saved and loaded with the patch
PatchNotes.notes: The text field is a LedDisplayTextField with multiline set to false, so it holds one line; the shipped Cable Colours preset stores its columns as spaces inside a single string.
